title: How elephant ears work as air-conditioners

scenes.headline: An elephant's ears are its air-conditioner.
Each ear is laced with blood vessels.
scenes.body: On hot days the elephant flaps its ears, and the moving air cools the blood inside them.

scenes.headline: Warm blood in. Cooler blood out.
scenes.body: The cooled blood flows back into the body and helps lower its temperature.

scenes.headline: After the bath: a coat of dust and mud.
scenes.body: Elephants cover themselves in dirt, sand and mud to protect their skin.

scenes.label: Asian elephants left in the wild (estimate)
scenes.source: Smithsonian's National Zoo; IUCN Red List

caption:
Elephant ears double as radiators.

Asian elephants are slightly smaller than their African cousins, and their ears are full of veins that let flapping cool the blood.

Sources: Smithsonian's National Zoo; IUCN Red List. Footage: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage, Sri Lanka (captive herd). Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Step-by-step mechanism told with a familiar metaphor (AC), ending on the species' status; orphanage footage shows normal bathing, not claimed as wild.
